newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pacific falls on placement plan.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pacific falls on placement plan.

text.p: Shares of COSCO Pacific Ltd fell on Tuesday on concerns about dilution after the company announced it would raise HK$1.2 billion in a share placement.
Brokers also said the company's 1996 profit was in line with expectations, prompting some profit-taking.
"Fears of dilution after the placement have given investors an excuse to take profit, in particular after its recent rise in price," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
COSCO shares were down HK$0.20 to HK$10.30 in early trade on Tuesday after a one-day trading suspension. Volume was 129.24 million shares worth HK$1.29 billion.

COSCO Pacific said on Monday it would raise HK$1.2 billion in a share placement at HK$9.95 per share to fund port acquisitions and the expansion of Chinese terminals and container manufacturing plants.
Li said the plans to use the proceeds for acquisitions and expansion had brightened COSCO Pacific's prospects.
"That will give support to the share price after a short-term correction," he said.
The company also reported a 63.3 percent rise in 1996 profit to US$75.7 million.
